distinguishing_features: Compliant polyurethane elastomer lining mechanically bonded to the elbow interior as a wear-dissipating layer
Curved transition lip at the elbow exit that re-attaches separated gas flow and reduces particle impingement angle
Viscoelastic energy dissipation that lowers transmitted peak contact stress to shift failure from abrasive cutting to impact fatigue
Hardware-level surface/geometry modification targeting the particle-impingement wear site directly
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce erosive wear-through of a pneumatic conveying elbow at the particle-impingement zone by lowering the transmitted impact stress and the particle impingement angle on the inner wall.
parsed.viable_reason: Compliant PU linings and elbow-exit flow-lip geometry are physically sound and proven anti-erosion approaches, feasible at the stated 3 mm lining thickness and 20 mm lip scale without exotic materials.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the cited prior art addresses hardware-level elbow erosion at all (they concern impeller-life prediction, flare-tip load capping, and electrochemical dosing), so combining viscoelastic compliance with a flow-reattachment lip to shift erosion physics is not an obvious derivation from the available closest art.
